topic: Fuel gauge reads wrong or bounces around: the sending unit, not the tank
mode: PRODUCTION (pack only, no live reel-canary call)
negativePrompt: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles

beats.narration: Your fuel gauge says empty right after you filled up, or it bounces around while you drive.
beats.visualPrompt: Macro shot, dashboard fuel gauge cluster, needle sitting near empty, subtle backlight glow, slow push-in, no hands or driver visible, shallow depth of field

beats.narration: That's usually not the tank. It's the sending unit, the float that tells the gauge how much fuel is left.
beats.visualPrompt: Cutaway-style macro shot of a fuel tank sending unit assembly on a workbench, float arm and resistor strip visible, static locked shot with subtle rack-focus shift, no hands

beats.narration: Inside the tank, a float rides the fuel level and moves a resistor. Years of fuel and vibration wear down that resistor's contact points, so the signal skips or reads wrong.
beats.visualPrompt: Close macro orbit around the sending unit's resistor strip and float arm, slight worn/oxidized texture visible on contact points, slow orbital camera move, no hands or text

beats.narration: A quick check: if the needle jumps when you hit a bump or take a turn, that's the sending unit talking, not a tank problem.
beats.visualPrompt: Macro shot of dashboard fuel needle mid-flutter, subtle vibration blur on the needle, car interior softly lit, no hands, no on-screen text

beats.narration: Don't just live with guessing your fuel level. Nick's Tire and Auto can check the sending unit and confirm it before you're stuck guessing at the pump.
beats.visualPrompt: Wide, warm-lit shot of a shop garage bay entrance, clean and inviting, static locked shot with subtle ambient depth-of-field breathing, no faces or logos
